source.title: RePAIR: Interactive Machine Unlearning through Prompt-Aware Model Repair
source.authors: Jagadeesh Rachapudi; Pranav Singh; Ritali Vatsi; Praful Hambarde; Amit Shukla

record.tranche_reason: Evaluates post-unlearning targeted-knowledge and retention performance for several unlearning methods, but uses no recovery attack.
record.gate_note: The study reports ordinary unlearning outcomes, not whether forgotten knowledge can be recovered. It does not test relearning fine-tuning, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompting attacks. The layer-separation value used to select Layer 7 is not recorded as a result row because it is used for method selection. Rows are limited to 60; omitted results are described in rows_left_out.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper proposing STAMP/STAMP-LR, a training-free, single-sample unlearning edit, inside the RePAIR pipeline. It reports only standard post-unlearning forget and retain scores for its method and six baselines. It runs no relearning, ablation, quantization or prompting attack and does not probe whether knowledge is deleted or merely blocked. Version A's contested point is that simple attacks don't recover the knowledge, so these numbers cannot bear on whether unlearning is shallow. Free-form Acc_f of 0.00, read as refusal-style outputs, is also not 'near chance' on the MCQ benchmark. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that STAMP and STAMP-LR reach near-zero forget scores (Acc_f 0.00, F-RL 0.00) while preserving utility, outperforming six baselines. They report up to ~3x speedup and say the RePAIR pipeline detects and satisfies user unlearning requests above 96%. They also report that baselines fail entirely in single-sample forgetting. They make no claim about robustness to recovery attacks.
record.recipe_differences: STAMP is a new training-free, single-sample method using pseudoinverse weight updates to redirect MLP activations toward a refusal subspace; it is not a reproduction of the listed unlearning recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome is reported across task, method, intervention layer, low-rank rank, forget-set size, and retain-buffer ratio. Rank below 64 is described as making unlearning incomplete, though Table 6 lists F-RL as 0.00 at each rank.
record.peer_reviewed: ACM MM ’26 is named in the paper header; the supplied venue is arXiv.org.
record.problems: No recovery attacks are performed, so the study cannot establish whether knowledge remains recoverable. No chance-level reference or uncertainty estimates are reported. Table 2's personal-data F-RL values for FLAT and WGA (0.33 and 0.45) conflict with the discussion's summary that all F-RL values are below 0.30. Table 6's zero F-RL values conflict with the text's statement that ranks below 64 yield incomplete unlearning.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit was reached. Omitted Table 2 retain-accuracy rows for FLAT, WGA, and ASU; Table 8 retain-accuracy rows for six training-based baselines; Table 6 runtime and utility results; and all Table 7 retain-ratio results. These were lower priority than the primary forget scores, selected retention comparisons, single-sample outcomes, and rank sweep.

untested.parts: Only ordinary forget and retain scores are reported. There is no attack testing whether the knowledge is recoverable, and no chance-level or MCQ reference.
No activation-direction ablation and no blocked-versus-deleted analysis, even though STAMP itself steers activations toward a refusal direction.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context probe.
STAMP is not claimed or tested to resist recovery attacks.

record.verdict_notes: The record's verdicts for A were dropped. The study's forget scores measure surface outputs after a refusal-steering edit, which is exactly the kind of evaluation the shallow-unlearning versions question. It provides no evidence either way on recoverability. STAMP adds a steering vector toward 'I don't know' activations at one MLP layer, a mechanism plausibly vulnerable to the attacks in C, but the paper does not test this.

versions.untested_parts: Tests ordinary post-unlearning targeted-knowledge and retention performance; does not test whether simple attacks recover knowledge. It also does not report a chance-level reference.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or other relearning attack is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or experiment distinguishing blocked access from deletion is reported.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery attack is tested.
STAMP and STAMP-LR are proposed as unlearning methods, not tested for resistance to the listed recovery attacks.
